reason: The passage opens the Book of Exodus, which is fundamentally the narrative of Yahweh's deliverance of the Hebrew people from slavery. While this particular excerpt does not contain an explicit divine statement of purpose, it demonstrates Yahweh's favor toward those who protect Hebrew lives: the midwives who fear God (וַתִּירֶאן הַֽמְיַלְּדוֹת אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים) are blessed by God (וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדוֹת), and the text preserves the narrative of Moses's deliverance through divine providence. The passage establishes the foundational context for the entire Exodus narrative, which centers on Yahweh's commitment to liberate the Hebrew people from Egyptian oppression. The theological framework of the passage—showing God's approval of those who act to preserve Hebrew lives—supports the broader biblical claim about Yahweh's goals.
